pull_requests.title: feat(ffe): preserve ordinary fallbacks for experimentation opt-out
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Implements ordinary fallback delivery from [RFC: Classifying allocations for per-subject experimentation opt-out](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit), **What exclusion means during evaluation**.

The agreed behavior skips experimental allocations before randomization and continues ordinary rules. The compiler currently removes those later rules after a full-population experiment.

### PR stack order

**Position:** Stack A, second PR. Solid arrows show Git parent → child. The dashed arrow shows a deployment prerequisite, not a Git parent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph A["Stack A: immediate opt-out compiler support"]
        W["#139368: winner logging"] --> F["#139379: retain fallbacks (this PR)"]
    end
    subgraph B["Stack B: stable activation metadata"]
        V["#139367: RC validation"] --> P["#139381: persist and publish"]
    end
    M["k8s-resources #12479: nullable storage"] -.-> P
```

| Stack goal | Review and merge order | Why stacked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A: preserve ordinary delivery during immediate opt-out.** | [#139368](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368) → [#139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379) | Correct winner classification first. The fallback optimizer then uses that classification to retain skippable experiments' fallbacks. |
| **B: provide stable activation times for future-experiments-only mode.** | [#139367](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139367) → [#139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) | Separate schema acceptance from emission, so validators can deploy before producers. |

Both stacks start from `main` and can progress independently. [Migration #12479](https://github.com/ddoghq/k8s-resources/pull/12479) targets `k8s-resources/master`. Deploy it and RC validation before #139381; merging alone is insufficient.

## Description

Retain later allocations and their variants until an ordinary full-population allocation makes them unreachable. Preserve evaluation reasons and assignments for subjects who remain eligible.

Completed ordinary winners still terminate the waterfall. Active experiments, including 100% enrollment and single-arm experiments, retain their fallback. This change adds no SDK configuration or telemetry.

For a full-population experiment, the compiled configuration must support both paths:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E["Active experiment: doLog = true"] -->|"Eligible subject"| R["Existing randomized assignment"]
    E -->|"Opted-out subject: skip"| F["Retained ordinary fallback"]
    F -->|"Matches"| O["Ordinary assignment"]
    F -->|"No match"| N["Continue remaining rules; existing no-assignment behavior"]
```

This PR preserves the rules. It does not add the evaluator's opt-out check.

### Later stacks: preview

These are planned follow-up groups, not additional published PRs in this series.

| Order | Goal | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C: complete activation coverage** | Establish usable activation metadata for supported allocation types. | Remaining lifecycle writers, canary/bandit coverage where supported, holdout timing, and missing-metadata behavior. |
| **D: shared fixtures and evaluators** | Apply the same cutoff rule locally and at the edge. | Timestamp fixtures first; Go/Rust evaluators, JSON/archive compatibility, Precompute transport, and cache handling. |
| **E: SDK delivery** | Let customers select future-experiments-only behavior consistently. | Extend existing opt-out integrations, pass the customer cutoff, and test request acknowledgement and cached-state compatibility. |

The existing immediate-mode SDK work does not wait for C–E. Future-mode enablement requires completed producer/consumer support and end-to-end validation; these five PRs do not enable it.

## How has this been tested?

The full UFC suite and `ffe-service` build pass. Differential cases compare 12,288 eligible-subject assignments and check ordinary fallback delivery after skipping experiments. JSON and protobuf retain the same allocation order. The holdout compiler-to-analysis regression passes, including its negative control for missing post-ship holdout exposures.

These tests do not exercise a deployed edge service or an SDK opt-out request.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Review the optimizer's reachability rule and evaluation-reason compatibility. Retained fallbacks increase configuration size when a logging allocation previously removed them.

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P2]** Removing this flag from the compatibility payload matches the SemVer policy we want. Please make the policy hold when the optimizer prunes the SEMVER rule too. The policy we want: a flag whose authored allocations contain a `SEMVER_*` condition goes only to the tracer versions in `semverSafeUFCTargets`, whether or not opt-out applies. A flag with an override serves one variant and skips this check (`ufc/compiler.go:206-247`). Those versions isolate a `SEMVER_*` condition to its flag (`remote-config/direct_client.go:35-49`). Every other tracer gets the payload that `FilterSemverFlags` builds. With the org rollout off, server builds already apply the policy to the allocations before optimization (`ufc/compiler.go:247-259`). `FilterSemverFlags` checks the optimized allocations instead (`ufc/semver_filter.go:45-58`). So a SEMVER rule after an ordinary full-population allocation, such as a completed winner or a 100% rollout, is pruned, and the flag still reaches the other tracers. The pruned rule can never match, so this is about one consistent rule, not about a tracer parsing an unsupported condition. Before this PR, the same gap applied after any full-population allocation. Now it applies only after one with `doLog=false` (`ufc/optimizer.go:127`).
Evidence — compiled through BuildFlagsConfiguration - The test below compiles an ordinary full-population allocation, then a `SEMVER_GTE` rule, with server SemVer enabled. At `1a71c67a` it fails: the flag stays in the compatibility payload. - With the one-line fix, it passes. `//domains/ffe/libs/flagging/ufc:go_default_test` (805 tests), `//domains/ffe/libs/flagging/remote-config:go_default_test` (108) and `//domains/ffe/apps/apis/feature-flagging-cache-worker:go_default_test` (84) pass.

pull_requests.title: fix(ffe): stop deterministic winner exposures while preserving holdouts
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Opted-out subjects should retain deterministic completed winners while skipping allocations that randomize. A retained experiment link keeps winners at `doLog=true`; clearing that field based only on experiment completion also lets completed 50/50 experiments bypass opt-out.

The [author clarification](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368#discussion_r4353896956) and [D018 producer contract](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/backend-feedback.md#d018-randomization-is-represented-by-dolog) require the backend to represent randomization through the existing `doLog` field. This refines the [original allocation-classification RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit).

## Description

Completed standard experiments (`ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` or `CODE_REMOVED`) stop ordinary winner exposures only when delivery is deterministic. The compiler sets `doLog=true` whenever shard selection changes the variation or match/fallthrough outcome, including ordinary percentage splits and partial enrollment. This deliberately enables exposures for ordinary randomized allocations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["Compiled allocation"] --> R["Randomizes variation or enrollment"]
    C --> W["Deterministic completed winner"]
    C --> H["Existing active experiment or holdout logging"]
    R --> T["doLog = true"]
    H --> T
    W --> F["doLog = false; eligible for delivery"]
```

Existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, and generated-holdout logging requirements are preserved, along with the experiment link, serial IDs, and assignments. Missing lifecycle state retains logging. Lifecycle state is read in one organization-scoped snapshot query using an array parameter. The synthetic holdout runner accepts either logging value for concluded winners while retaining winner and active-experiment checks.

This PR is the Git parent of [#139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379), which must inherit this change before fallback validation. [Activation metadata #139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) and [edge opt-out #140422](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/140422) have separate rollout work. Deploy the compiler and rebuild stored UFCs before enabling consumers; newly logging allocations without activation metadata retain conservative future-mode exclusion.

## How has this been tested?

After merging main at [0ae33d8f11](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/0ae33d8f112685502bb8f16d8c96efbecb70219b), 918 compiler tests, 283 database repository tests, and 275 holdout-runner/primary-analysis tests pass locally. Main's golden snapshot required seven intentional `doLog` updates; all assignment data remains unchanged. The classifier matches independent raw-bucket enumeration for 500 generated cases. Restoring the old `doLog` output fails the completed 50/50, ordinary 50/50, and partial-enrollment regressions; restoring the fix passes both Go suites uncached.

[Draft contract #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) retains the source pins, negative controls, and native receipts. Seven new Lean composition theorems bring its audit to 53, with 313 existing semantic cases and 36 operational cases passing. These prove the model's composition; native classifier correctness is covered separately by the compiler tests. Handler lifecycle tests and the combined edge flow were not rerun in this update; local validation is not deployed proof.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Review the randomization classification, preservation of deterministic winner delivery and holdout exposures, and organization-scoped snapshot query. Confirm D018's exposure-logging consequence for ordinary randomized allocations and retain the separate rollout gates.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P1]** A concluded standard experiment that still splits traffic now compiles with `doLog=false`, so it randomizes opted-out subjects. Please base opt-out eligibility on randomization, not on `doLog` alone. We want a concluded experiment to behave like a randomized allocation that was never an experiment, and we want opted-out subjects to skip both, because both randomize. The exclusion in #140422 checks only `doLog`, so it skips neither. The RFC reuses `doLog` alone, so this needs a product decision. This line derives `doLog` for standard experiments from experiment state alone. That adds a new way to reach the state above: the deprecated PATCH `experiment_action: CONCLUDED` sets `ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` without rolling out the winner (`experiment_service.go:653`, called from `experiment_handler.go:2584`). The allocation keeps its split and now compiles with `doLog=false`. I put the evaluator-side change in my comment on #140422 at `experimentation.rs:62`.
Evidence — 1. a completed standard experiment that still splits compiles with doLog=false I added a `TestWinnerExposureLifecycle` row at `3e99ba2a`: a standard experiment with `completed: true` and weights 50/50. The compiled allocation has `doLog=false`, and the split stays.
Evidence — 2. callers still send the deprecated field `ffe.experimentation.experiment.patch_lifecycle_deprecated{field:experiment_action}`, summed over the 30 days to 2026-10-21: us1 95, eu1 28, us5 17, us3 13. The handler counts each request before later checks can reject it (`experiment_handler.go:2259-2264`), and the metric records neither the action nor the outcome. So these are requests that set the field, not successful concludes.
Evidence — 3. opted-out subjects are randomized A probe on the #140422 evaluators, in immediate mode, with a `doLog=false` allocation that splits 50/50 between two variations before a fallback: 200 opted-out subjects got `a` 106 and `b` 94, and none reached the fallback. The JSON and archived evaluators agree on every subject.

🤖 **Comment from Codex working with Leo:** **Decision [D018, revision 1](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018): the backend must represent randomization through the existing `doLog` field.** Thanks, Aaron — agreed that a completed experiment can still randomize. We’re keeping allocations that randomize subject to opt-out, including ordinary percentage splits and partial enrollment. The backend owns that classification; evaluators retain the existing `doLog` predicate and future-mode cutoff rule. This records Leo’s clarification in [this decision thread](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368#discussion_r4343813763); the earlier withdrawn selection remains in [provenance](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/local-decision.json). **Implemented in [d0a2de5b58](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/d0a2de5b58dba158941d2c2f81016276a45ea2c1); validated after merging main at [0ae33d8f11](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/0ae33d8f112685502bb8f16d8c96efbecb70219b).** The compiler sets `doLog=true` when shard selection changes the variation or match/fallthrough outcome. Deterministic completed winners remain `false`, while existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, and holdout logging requirements are preserved. **Shared proofs:** [draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) contains the [D018 decision](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018), its Lean proofs, and the linked validation history.
Behavior — the distinction we are preserving | Allocation | Compiler output | Immediate mode with a valid subject cutoff | | --- | --- | --- | | Completed experiment still splitting 50/50 | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Ordinary percentage split | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Single variant with partial percentage enrollment | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Deterministic completed ordinary winner | `doLog=false` | Remains eligible for delivery. | | Existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, or generated-holdout logging | Preserve the existing logging requirement. | Skip when `doLog=true`. | This deliberately enables exposure logging for ordinary randomized allocations. Targeting rules and time windows do not themselves make an allocation random; changing between match and fallthrough does. First-match order, unreachable variants, empty ranges, and same-variant coverage are handled by the native classifier. Future mode keeps its strictly-before cutoff rule: earlier activation remains eligible, while unknown activation is conservatively excluded. Deployment still requires the fallback-preserving child, regenerated UFCs, and activation coverage for newly logging allocations.
Native validation — local checks at 0ae33d8f11 - **918 compiler tests, 283 database repository tests, and 275 runner/primary-analysis tests pass.** The [merged-source receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/main-merge-native-validation.json) records the commands, source hashes, and exact execution scope. The repository run preceded only the compiler-test snapshot/comment correction; its library source was unchanged. - The classifier matches **500 independent raw-bucket enumeration cases**, alongside targeted cases for partial enrollment, first-match ordering, unreachable variants, and same-variant coverage. - Before main integration, restoring the old `doLog` output failed the completed 50/50, ordinary 50/50, and partial-enrollment regressions. The [negative-control receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/native-validation.json) retains its original source and patch pins; restoring the fix passed both Go suites uncached. - Main introduced a golden snapshot with seven old `doLog=false` expectations. That initial failure is preserved in [V052](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#v052). Updating only those seven logging bits leaves **every assignment field unchanged**; the subsequent compiler run passes, recorded in [V053](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#v053). These are local native checks. The model proof does not establish correctness of the Go partition classifier. Child-stack integration, CI, and deployed behavior remain separate evidence.
Sneak preview — turning review decisions into reusable, checked contracts The shared decisions and proofs are published in **[draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55)** at [99854cf878](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/commit/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34): 1. **[A versioned English decision — D018, revision 1](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018)**, linked to where it was set. 2. **[An executable Lean model and checked proofs](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/BackendReview.lean#L6-L41)** of the producer/evaluator composition. 3. **[The existing semantic corpus](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/corpus/browser-proposal.jsonl)** and **[operational corpus](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/corpus/inactive-path.jsonl)**, preserving the broader opt-out contract. These are not new D018 producer-classification cases; the classifier has separate native enumeration and regression tests. 4. **[A linked history of evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#historical-linked-checks)**, preserving passing and failing checks separately from the decision’s authority. For example, [this theorem](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/BackendReview.lean#L26-L28) is checked in the published model: ```lean theorem immediate_excludes_randomized_allocations (existingExposure : Bool) : (compiledPolicy .immediate .valid .missing existingExposure true).exclude = true := by cases existingExposure <;> rfl ``` In plain English: within this model, an allocation classified as randomized is excluded in immediate mode with a valid subject cutoff, even without an existing exposure-logging requirement. The modeled compiler combines the two requirements as `existingExposure || randomized`; it does not infer randomization from native shard data. The [model validation](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/model-validation.json) passes **53 theorem audits**, including seven new D018 theorems, plus **313 existing semantic cases and 36 operational cases**. A separate theorem distinguishes the old non-logging split from the corrected producer contract. The useful result is a reviewable rule with a source-pinned evidence trail. The Lean proof establishes properties of the model; the [native receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/main-merge-native-validation.json) establishes the bounded compiler checks above. The central PR remains a draft, and fleet adoption remains a separate decision.

<sub><sub>![P1](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub> **Exposure-event logging is forced on fleet-wide for all randomized allocations with no kill switch**

This unconditionally ORs `splitsRandomize(result.Splits)` into `LogExposureEvent` for every compiled allocation, including plain percentage splits and every progressive-rollout step produced by `BuildSyntheticAllocationConfigurations` (whose exposure sharder makes partial enrollment randomize). Today none of those allocation types log exposures — only experiment, canary, and bandit allocations do. Once UFCs are rebuilt, SDKs across every org will start emitting exposure events for all percentage rollouts in a single step, which can significantly increase load on exposure intake and the downstream pipeline, and the only way back is a code revert plus another fleet-wide UFC rebuild.

This is a behavior change with fleet-wide blast radius and no runtime kill switch, so it isn't safely expressible as a minimal line-level code suggestion — it needs a design change. Recommend gating the `splitsRandomize` OR-in behind a runtime flag that can be enabled per org or by percentage (defaulting to the current/old behavior), with the compiler reading that flag so it can be disabled without a redeploy. Keep the `ExperimentRolloutComplete` change (already in this diff, a few lines above) separate, since it is a distinct, narrower fix that lets completed deterministic winners stop logging. Before widely enabling the new flag, confirm exposure intake has capacity for the added volume.

React with 👍 / 👎 or respond to this suggestion!
